1. Purpose of the Assignment
This assignment is designed to make students prepare and use a working Python environment, apply
fundamental Python programming concepts, use Python libraries, develop and test programs, and
communicate their work through a group presentation. The practical work follows the handout's
progression from preparing the Python environment to developing Python concepts and scripts.
2. Important Instructions
• This is group work for development and presentation; however, every student must participate
actively.
• EVERY STUDENT MUST COME WITH A COMPUTER and must be able to run Python on that
computer.
• Before starting the programming tasks, each student must configure the Python environment and
install/verify the required libraries.
• The group must not rely on only one member's computer. During assessment, any member may be
asked to demonstrate a task on his/her computer.
• All members must understand the submitted code and be ready to explain or modify part of it during
the presentation.
• Keep evidence of environment configuration, commands, code execution, outputs, errors corrected,
and final results.
• Use the supplied AI with Python handout as the main learning reference for the assignment.
3. Part A - Individual Computer and Python Environment Preparation
Before the group starts the main programming work, EVERY MEMBER must complete the following
on his/her own computer.
A1. Verify/Install Python
1. Check whether Python 3 is installed. If it is not installed, install it.
2. Verify the installed Python version from Command Prompt/Terminal.
3. Ensure Python can be executed from the command line and correct the PATH if necessary.

4. Keep a screenshot showing successful Python version verification.
A2. Configure a Development Tool
5. Install or configure a suitable Python editor/IDE such as Visual Studio Code, PyCharm, Jupyter
Notebook/JupyterLab, or another appropriate environment.
6. Create a working folder named AI_With_Python_Assignment.
A3. Verify PIP and Install Libraries
7. Verify that PIP is available and display its version.
8. Use PIP to install the libraries required by your group's work.
9. At minimum, for the data/AI activities prepare NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and scikit-learn.
10. Create environment_test.py, import the installed libraries, run it, and confirm that no import error
occurs.
11. Keep screenshots of the important commands and successful execution.
4. Part B - Python Fundamentals Practical
Develop a small Student Performance Program. It must request a student's name and marks for at least
three subjects, store the values using appropriate variables/data types, calculate total and average, and
display well-formatted results.
• Use input and output statements.
• Demonstrate variables and appropriate data types.
• Use arithmetic, comparison and logical operators where appropriate.
• Use conditional statements to classify performance (for example: Excellent, Very Good, Good, Pass
or Fail).
• Reject or handle invalid marks such as values below 0 or above 100.
• Use comments to make important parts of the code understandable.
5. Part C - Collections and Repetition
Extend the program to process several students and demonstrate the collection concepts covered in the
handout.
• Use a loop to process more than one student.
• Use an appropriate list, tuple, set and/or dictionary in meaningful parts of the solution.
• Display all stored student records.
• Determine the highest and lowest average.
• Calculate the overall class average.
• Count students who pass and fail.
• Be prepared to explain why each selected collection is appropriate.
6. Part D - File Handling and Exception Handling
• Save processed student results to a file.
• Read the saved results back and display them.

• Use appropriate file modes for reading/writing.
• Use try/except where appropriate so that common input or file errors do not simply crash the
program.
• Document at least one error encountered during development and explain how the group corrected it.
7. Part E - Python Libraries, Data Analysis and Visualization
Using the results produced by the program or an instructor-approved dataset:
• Load and organize data using pandas and/or NumPy.
• Calculate useful summary information.
• Produce at least one clear Matplotlib graph comparing student performance.
• Add a meaningful title and axis labels to the graph.
• Write a short interpretation of what the graph shows.
8. Part F - Introductory AI/Machine Learning Practical
Using an instructor-approved dataset, demonstrate a simple machine-learning workflow with scikitlearn. The purpose is to show that the group can connect Python programming and libraries to an
introductory AI task.
12. Load the dataset.
13. Identify the input feature(s) and target/output.
14. Check the data and prepare it as required.
15. Separate features from the target.
16. Split the data into training and testing sets.
17. Select and train one appropriate simple machine-learning model.
18. Generate predictions and evaluate them using an appropriate metric.
19. Explain, in simple terms, what the obtained result means.
9. Group Presentation
Each group will present and demonstrate its work. The presentation must be practical: slides may
support the explanation, but the group must also run the programs and show evidence from members'
computers.
Presentation Section
Expected Content
1. Introduction
Problem/task, group members and what the group
developed.
2. Environment Preparation
Python version, IDE, PATH/PIP configuration
and installed libraries.
3. Python Concepts Used
Variables, data types, operators, conditions, loops
and collections.
4. Program Demonstration
Run the student performance program and
explain the main logic.
5. File Handling & Errors
Show saved/read data and explain one handled
error.

6. Data Analysis & Graph
Show the analysis and interpret the graph.
7. AI/ML Demonstration
Explain features/target, training/testing, model,
prediction and evaluation.
8. Challenges & Conclusion
What was difficult, how it was solved, and what
the group learned.
10. Participation Requirement
IMPORTANT: The presentation is a GROUP presentation, but marks should reflect individual
participation. Every member must present or demonstrate a meaningful part. The facilitator may select
any member to explain code, run the program, identify a library, explain an error, or make a small
modification.
11. What the Group Must Submit
• One organized group assignment folder.
• Python source files (.py) and/or notebook files (.ipynb).
• Dataset(s) used, where applicable.
• Generated result/data files.
• Graph(s) produced by the program.
• requirements.txt listing required external libraries.
• Presentation slides.
• Evidence/screenshots showing that group members prepared their Python environments.
• A short README file identifying group members and explaining how to run the project.
